title: 6 Month Check-in for New Service Providers
overview:
As part of the accreditation process, Contracted Service Providers (providers) agree they will have certain policies and procedures in place to meet requirements of the Australian Government Hearing Services Program (the program) prior to claiming services.

The 6 Month Check-in survey has been developed to assist providers with understanding if they are meeting requirements.

The survey will take you through common areas that we receive enquiries about and ask you to provide copies of policies, procedures and forms your business has in place.

Please take time to read and understand the contents of the survey.

title: OGTR Cost Recovery Implementation Statement
overview:
The Gene Technology Regulator has prepared a draft Cost Recovery Implementation Statement (CRIS) to ensure transparency and accountability for the level of charging and to demonstrate that the purpose for charging is being achieved. The draft CRIS and supporting documents outline cost recovery activities, how fees and charges are calculated, timelines and how stakeholders can provide their feedback. The draft CRIS and other relevant documents can be viewed in the related attachments below.

We value stakeholder feedback and encourage interested parties to provide their views. The insights gathered through this consultation will help inform program and implementation considerations.

title: Specialist Affordability: Options to Address Excessive Fees
overview:
The Australian Government is committed to making sure Australians have transparency, choice and affordable access to private specialist medical care. However, we know Australians are paying increasingly higher fees to see medical specialists, and many are delaying or missing care as a result.

The Government is currently undertaking work to examine variation in fees for specialist medical services. The outcome of this consultation will inform our development of methods to identify "excessive" fees for specialist medical services, and identify opportunities for intervention to protect patients.
